methodological_rigor.justification: A retrospective single-center study of 170 consecutive MPLC patients undergoing secondary pulmonary resection with a clearly defined PPC composite endpoint and QCT-derived PPO-FEV1%pred using a specific attenuation range (-910 to -600 HU). The 52 PPC events support only a small multivariable logistic model (~5 events per variable), and a total of 15-16 variables were significant in univariate testing with backward elimination, raising concerns about overfitting despite bootstrap internal validation. Cutoffs were derived by Youden's index in the same cohort (no split-sample) and the Abstract contains a clear error stating 'no significant differences...(P<0.05)' (the Results instead shows P<0.05 differences existed). Statistical confidence intervals on one-lung ventilation time (OR 1.009, 95% CI 1.000-1.019) include unity, undermining the claim of independence.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort (LoE 2b) addressing a niche but practical question: identifying patients with MPLC at elevated PPC risk before a second resection. QCT-based PPO-FEV1%pred cutoff of ~79.45% could plausibly inform risk stratification and perioperative optimization, but as the authors note, the high-altitude cohort and single-center thresholds limit direct generalizability without external validation.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prediction-model development study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard; most key elements are present (participants, predictors, outcome definition, model-building approach, internal validation, calibration via HL test and calibration slope) but several TRIPOD items are missing: explicit handling of missing data, predictor measurement blinding, full regression coefficients/intercept for Model 1 and Model 2 to enable replication, and sample-size justification. No data or code availability, no TRIPOD checklist, no registration.

novelty_literature.justification: Applying QCT-derived PPO-FEV1%pred specifically to secondary resection in MPLC, and incorporating postoperative pain at 48 h as an early risk marker, is a targeted extension of prior work (Kobayashi 2017; Fernández-Rodríguez 2018) that used 3D-CT volumetry for first-resection PPO prediction. The novelty is incremental, confirming and extending existing methods in a specific clinical population.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript has multiple clarity issues: the Abstract contains a contradictory statement (univariate showed 'no significant differences' then lists items 'P<0.05'); Results duplicates the pre-/intraoperative and augmented Model 2 descriptions across main analysis and sensitivity analysis; several figures (3-10) have legend texts that are near-duplicates; typographical errors ('sensivity' twice); and non-idiomatic phrasing throughout ('optimistically calibrated AUC'). Tables are reasonable but the Results text and Abstract are internally inconsistent in a way that obscures the actual findings.

key_strengths: Focused clinically relevant question on PPC prediction specifically for secondary resection in MPLC, an under-studied population
Use of QCT-derived functional lung volumes to compute PPO parameters offers a more individualized alternative to segment-count formulas that assume uniform lung function
Inclusion of bootstrap internal validation, calibration slope, and Hosmer-Lemeshow testing for two nested models (pre/intraoperative and early postoperative augmented)
Transparent discussion of altitude-specific limitations and need for external validation
key_concerns: Abstract contains a clear contradiction: claims univariate analysis revealed no significant differences while citing P<0.05 in the same sentence, which materially misrepresents the findings
Modest event count (52 PPCs) with many candidate predictors tested and backward elimination raises overfitting risk; events-per-variable ~5 is below recommended thresholds
OR 95% CI for one-lung ventilation time (1.000-1.019) includes unity, yet the variable is reported as an 'independent' predictor
Substantial duplicated text between main and sensitivity Model 1/Model 2 subsections and multiple typographical errors ('sensivity') suggest incomplete editorial review
No external validation, no regression coefficients provided for the final models, no TRIPOD checklist or data/code sharing
Cutoffs derived and optimized in the same single-center altitude cohort; generalizability explicitly unverified
chief_reviewer.rationale: A narrowly scoped single-center retrospective prediction study with useful clinical framing but notable internal inconsistencies, reporting lapses, and overfitting risk; fits a lower-tier specialty journal only after major revisions resolving abstract/text inconsistencies and strengthening reporting.
